title: Maximum Size Subarray Sum Equals k
description:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the maximum length of a contiguous subarray that sums to `k`. If there is no such subarray, return `0`.

A subarray is a contiguous non-empty sequence of elements within an array.
hints: Because nums can contain negative numbers and zeros, a standard sliding window does not apply directly.
Maintain a running prefix sum: a subarray ending at index i sums to k if and only if some earlier prefix sum equaled (prefixSum - k).

Use a hash map storing only the earliest index where each prefix sum occurs (initialized with {0: -1}) so that i - map[prefixSum - k] is maximized. Use 64-bit integers for prefix sums in fixed-width languages.

examples.explanation: The subarray [1, -1, 5, -2] sums to 3 and has length 4, which is the longest possible.
The subarray [-1, 2] sums to 1 and has length 2, which is the longest possible.
No contiguous subarray sums to 7, so return 0.
